newsitem.title: USA: CKE sees Hardee's deal accretive in FY98.
newsitem.headline: CKE sees Hardee's deal accretive in FY98.

text.p: CKE Restaurants Inc said Monday it expects its acquisition of the Hardee's fast-food chain from Imasco Ltd will be accretive to earnings in its current fiscal year, ending January 1998.
"It is expected to be accretive in the fiscal year we are now in," CKE spokesman Loren Pannier told Reuters. "We are not quantifying it at this point."
Pannier said there will be "selective store closures" of Hardee's restaurants although he said it was too soon to say how many.
"The whole idea is to fix the problem rather than close stores," he said.
Pannier said the deal is expected to close in CKE's second quarter and it will start working with Hardee's management immediately to make improvements.
He said the deal will be financed through a combination of a secondary common stock offering, notes and a bank loan.

Pannier said CKE plans to do a secondary offering of its common stock to net $100 million and will also issue $50 million in convertible notes to Imasco. The notes will be convertible into CKE common stock when CKE stock price appreciates by about 22 percent to 25 percent.
The balance will be funded through a bank loan from Banque Paribas, he said.
